subject: Civil Engineering
title: Risk Management in Construction
description: A short lesson to help you apply Risk Management in Construction.

hook.text: Rain, strikes, supply shortages, and design errors — construction is full of uncertainty.

buildup.text: Risk identification lists every possible threat — technical, financial, schedule, and external.

discovery.text: Risk assessment rates each by probability and impact — creating a prioritized risk register.

twist.text: Insurance transfers some risks — but not delays, design errors, or contractor disputes.

climax.text: COVID-19 shut down construction globally — a risk almost no project had planned for.

punchline.text: Risk can be managed but never eliminated. The best plans include what could go wrong.

quiz.question: What does a construction risk register contain?
options: A list of all workers and their qualifications
Identified risks rated by probability and impact, prioritized for management
The schedule of all inspections required by the building code

details.summary: Construction risk management systematically identifies, analyzes, and responds to threats that could affect project objectives. Common risks include weather delays, unforeseen soil conditions, labor shortages, material price escalation, design changes, and regulatory delays.
details.whyItMatters: Construction projects face more uncertainty than most other industries due to unique site conditions, weather exposure, and complex supply chains. Proactive risk management prevents surprises from becoming crises.
takeaways: Risk identification uses checklists, brainstorming, and historical project data
Risk response strategies include avoid, mitigate, transfer, and accept
Contingency reserves provide financial and schedule buffers for realized risks

faq.question: What are the most common risks in construction projects?
faq.answer: Weather delays, unforeseen ground conditions, labor shortages, material price escalation, design errors and omissions, subcontractor default, regulatory delays, and scope changes are consistently the highest risks.

faq.question: How much contingency should a construction project budget include?
faq.answer: Contingency typically ranges from 5 to 15% for well-defined projects to 25 to 50% for early-stage estimates or complex projects. The amount should be based on quantitative risk analysis rather than arbitrary percentages.
